reason: Refuted as written. The bookkeeping idea is harmless, but three parts are wrong or redundant. (1) REDUNDANT: exp70g 56606948 is already on the private-read list (CONTEXT l.3056 item (8)), and so is every 28/29 Sep ref (l.3195 item (10)); exp70q and exp78a are covered too. Only the prior and the joint-read rule are new. (2) MISCALIBRATED PRIOR: the private read is taken over the DISPLAYED 3-decimal contrasts (l.2289, l.2573: 'displayed contrasts in thousandths'). The L6/L7 priors already carry P(=0) .40/.45 for this reason. The registered .48/.04/.48 counts only exact zeros and is symmetric, although the finding's own MC mean is +0.0004. Simulating the 3-dp display with the r20pv-1 MC (mu +4e-4, sd 2e-3, 4% exact-zero mass) gives P(<0/=0/>0) ~.31/.23/.46; at half scale (sd 1e-3) it gives ~.19/.37/.44. A pre-registration with the wrong zero mass would score any '0' read as a 4% surprise. (3) CONFOUNDED CONTRAST: C_q = exp70q - exp70b mixes cap 6 with DIVINS_THRESH 0.3 (exp70q = K2 + cap 6 + thr 0.3 + fm45, l.2948), so it is not a cap read. (4) OVERSTATED INFERENCE: one pooled private draw cannot 'set' the public-like weight. The sign's likelihood ratio between the public-like hypothesis (P>0 ~.59) and the lab-like one (~.31) is only ~2 per non-zero read, and a '0' (~22%) says nothing. MEDAL VALUE: none, since this is post-deadline calibration. FEASIBILITY: trivial, with no runtime, R8 or dummy issue.
